items.prompt: Why is increasing j the safe in-place overwrite order when rolling one value row backward?

options.text: The needed old child at j+1 has not yet been overwritten.
options.why: Writing values[j] leaves both old children available for the current calculation.

options.text: Time itself moves forward during valuation.
options.why: Tree time moves backward; array overwrite order is a separate concern.

options.text: Decreasing j always computes the same rounded child data.
options.why: It can read an already overwritten up-child and change the recurrence.

options.text: Only a single terminal payoff is ever stored.
options.why: The rolling row holds up to N+1 node values.

items.explanation: Writing values[j] leaves both old children available for the current calculation.
